caption: The drawing depicts two tomahawk pipes, each rendered in colored pencil on a beige paper background. The top tomahawk pipe features a metal axe head shaded in grey and blue tones with hints of purple, attached to a wooden handle decorated with patterns in yellow, green, red, and purple. The handle is long and tapers toward the end, displaying alternating geometric and diagonal line patterns colored in muted earthy hues. The lower tomahawk pipe has a brass-colored head, depicted with yellow and green shades, featuring a rounded knob at the end and engraved leaf patterns visible on the axe blade. Its handle is brown with a subtle gradient, appearing more uniform and less decorated than the top handle. Handwritten notes accompany both illustrations, identifying them as belonging to the Ojibway Tribe, with additional details about their exhibition location, materials, and dimensions; both are signed and dated “Nov. 6, 1925, Mary Bremer.”
title: Tomahawk Pipe
